title: Knowledge check: Writing Custom Directives

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Writing Custom Directives”?
options: Put multi-step business logic directly in template expressions.
Use raw HTML rendering for every value.
Use declarative template bindings and keep expressions small; choose directives according to the intended DOM behavior.
Manually rewrite the DOM for every state change.
questions.answer_key: Use declarative template bindings and keep expressions small; choose directives according to the intended DOM behavior.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Writing Custom Directives directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “When a custom directive is useful”, which practice is most reliable?
options: Use raw HTML rendering for every value.
Use declarative template bindings and keep expressions small; choose directives according to the intended DOM behavior.
Manually rewrite the DOM for every state change.
Put multi-step business logic directly in template expressions.
questions.answer_key: Use declarative template bindings and keep expressions small; choose directives according to the intended DOM behavior.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “When a custom directive is useful”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Writing Custom Directives” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.
